title: Catalyst SYS LED amber - POST or hardware fault
shortDescription: The chassis SYS LED is solid amber, indicating power-on self-test failure or hardware error.
fullDescription:
On Catalyst 9200/9300/9500 series switches and ISR/ASR routers, a steady amber SYS LED means the device detected a hardware fault during POST or runtime. Common triggers include power supply failure, fan tray failure, or a stack member that failed to boot.

Connect via console (9600 8N1) and run 'show environment all' and 'show post' to identify the failed component. If the LED is blinking amber, the system is still booting or recovering and should be allowed to finish before troubleshooting.

Most field-replaceable units (PSU, fan tray, SFPs) can be hot-swapped. A persistent amber after replacement usually indicates a supervisor or motherboard failure requiring TAC RMA.

causes.cause: Power supply or fan tray failure
Failed POST diagnostics on a line card

fixSteps.title: Connect console
fixSteps.instruction: Plug a console cable into the RJ45/USB console port and open a terminal at 9600 8N1.

fixSteps.title: Check environment
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show environment all' and 'show post' to locate the failing FRU.

fixSteps.title: Reseat or replace FRU
fixSteps.instruction: Power down, reseat the indicated PSU, fan tray, or line card. Replace if reseat does not clear the fault.

fixSteps.title: Open TAC case if persistent
fixSteps.instruction: If amber persists after FRU replacement, collect 'show tech-support' and open a TAC RMA case.

whenToCallPro: Call Cisco TAC if SmartNet covered or persistent supervisor faults appear.
videoSearchQuery: Cisco Catalyst SYS LED amber troubleshoot

faq.q: Is blinking amber the same as solid?
faq.a: No - blinking amber means the system is booting or running diagnostics; wait 5 minutes before troubleshooting.
Yes on dual-PSU models. Single-PSU chassis require shutdown.

title: Meraki MX/MR solid orange - cannot reach dashboard
shortDescription: Meraki device LED is solid orange, indicating the device cannot reach the Meraki cloud dashboard.
fullDescription:
Meraki MX security appliances and MR access points use a single status LED. Solid orange means the device booted but cannot establish a connection to the Meraki cloud (dashboard.meraki.com). The device falls back to its last known config but cannot receive updates.

Most cases are upstream WAN problems: no DHCP, blocked outbound HTTPS to Meraki cloud, or DNS resolution failures. Meraki devices need outbound TCP 443/7734/9350-9354 to *.meraki.com and NTP UDP 123.

If WAN is healthy but the LED stays orange, the device may be claimed to a different organization or have a corrupt firmware. A 30-second factory reset (paperclip in reset hole) restores defaults.

causes.cause: Firewall blocking outbound HTTPS to Meraki cloud

fixSteps.title: Verify WAN
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a laptop to the WAN port and confirm DHCP/internet works.

fixSteps.title: Test cloud reachability
fixSteps.instruction: From a device on the same WAN, browse to https://dashboard.meraki.com - should load.

fixSteps.title: Open required ports
fixSteps.instruction: Whitelist outbound TCP 443, 7734, 9350-9354 and UDP 123 to *.meraki.com on upstream firewall.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset button 30 seconds with paperclip. Re-claim in dashboard.

whenToCallPro: Call Meraki support if device shows orange after factory reset and confirmed WAN connectivity.

faq.a: Yes - the device runs on its last config but won't get updates.

title: Router stuck in ROMMON prompt
shortDescription: Device boots into ROMMON instead of IOS, indicating IOS image is missing or corrupt.
fullDescription:
The 'rommon 1>' prompt appears when an IOS/IOS-XE router cannot find a valid boot image. On Catalyst switches the equivalent is the 'switch:' prompt. Causes include a deleted bootflash image, corrupt config-register (0x0 forces ROMMON), or failed firmware upgrade.

From ROMMON you can list bootflash with 'dir bootflash:', set the image with 'BOOT=bootflash:image.bin', and boot manually with 'boot'. If no image exists, use 'tftpdnld' to recover via TFTP server on the management port.

After recovery, set 'config-register 0x2102' from IOS exec mode and save - this prevents the device from dropping into ROMMON on reboot.

causes.cause: Missing or corrupt IOS image on bootflash

symptoms: rommon 1> or switch: prompt on console

fixSteps.title: List bootflash
fixSteps.instruction: At rommon prompt run 'dir bootflash:' and identify a valid .bin image.

fixSteps.title: TFTP recovery if no image
fixSteps.instruction: Set IP_ADDRESS, TFTP_SERVER, TFTP_FILE then run 'tftpdnld' from management port.

fixSteps.title: Fix config-register
fixSteps.instruction: From IOS exec: 'config-register 0x2102', then 'write memory' and reload.

whenToCallPro: Engage TAC if TFTP recovery fails or bootflash shows read errors.

faq.a: 0x2102 for normal boot. 0x2142 ignores startup-config (used for password recovery).

faq.q: Do I need a special TFTP server?
faq.a: Any TFTP server works - tftpd64 on Windows or in.tftpd on Linux.

title: Stack member in version-mismatch mode
shortDescription: A new stack member is running a different IOS version than the active and is in V-Mismatch state.
fullDescription:
When a Catalyst 9300/3850 stack adds a member with a different IOS-XE version, the new switch enters Version-Mismatch (V-M) mode. It does not forward traffic but joins the stack control plane.

Run 'show switch' to see members in 'V-Mismatch' state. Use 'software auto-upgrade enable' in global config so the active automatically pushes its image to mismatched members. Alternatively, manually run 'request platform software package install switch all file flash:image.bin auto-copy'.

The member reloads automatically once the image installs. Total upgrade typically takes 10-15 minutes per switch.

causes.cause: New switch added with factory IOS version
Insufficient flash space for new image
Mixed install vs bundle boot mode

symptoms: Stack port LEDs green but no forwarding on member

fixSteps.title: Verify mismatch
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show switch' and 'show version' on each member to confirm version difference.

fixSteps.title: Enable auto-upgrade
fixSteps.instruction: Configure 'software auto-upgrade enable' in global config.

fixSteps.title: Trigger install
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'request platform software package install switch all file flash:packages.conf auto-copy' from active.

fixSteps.title: Verify stack
fixSteps.instruction: After auto-reload, confirm 'show switch' shows all members 'Ready'.

whenToCallPro: Engage TAC if auto-upgrade fails or stack splits during upgrade.
videoSearchQuery: Cisco Catalyst stack version mismatch fix

faq.q: Will the stack keep forwarding during upgrade?
faq.a: Yes - active and ready members forward traffic; only the V-Mismatch member is offline.
Yes but downgrading the active is disruptive - upgrading the new member is preferred.

title: Fan tray failure on Catalyst chassis
shortDescription: Syslog reports a failed fan and chassis temperature is rising.
fullDescription:
The %FAN-3-FAN_FAILED syslog message indicates one or more fans in the fan tray have stopped or are spinning below the minimum RPM threshold. The FAN LED on the front panel turns amber. If multiple fans fail, thermal protection will shut down line cards or the entire chassis after 3 minutes.

Fan trays are field-replaceable on Catalyst 9400/9500/9600 and most ISR/ASR routers. They can be hot-swapped within a 60-second window without losing forwarding. After replacement the syslog clears and 'show environment fan' reports OK.

If the new fan tray also fails, the issue may be in the chassis fan controller or backplane and requires RMA.

causes.cause: Fan motor failure from age or dust

fixSteps.title: Confirm fault
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show environment fan' and 'show environment temperature' to confirm fan and current temps.

fixSteps.title: Hot-swap fan tray
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen captive screws, slide out failed tray, slide in replacement within 60 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Verify clear
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 30 seconds then run 'show environment fan' - all fans should report OK.

fixSteps.title: Clean intake filter
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum or replace intake filter to prevent recurrence.

whenToCallPro: Replacement fan tray also fails - chassis backplane may need RMA.

faq.q: How long can the chassis run with a failed fan?
faq.a: Typically 3-5 minutes before thermal shutdown - replace ASAP.
Yes within a 60-second window; longer outages trigger thermal protection.

title: OSPF adjacency flapping
shortDescription: OSPF neighbor repeatedly transitions between FULL and DOWN states.
fullDescription:
The %OSPF-5-ADJCHG syslog reports neighbor state changes. Frequent FULL -> DOWN transitions indicate adjacency instability, usually due to layer-1/2 issues, MTU mismatch, or hello/dead timer mismatch.

Check 'show ip ospf neighbor' and 'show ip ospf interface' for hello/dead intervals on both ends - they must match exactly. MTU mismatches manifest as adjacency stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE before dropping. Use 'ip ospf mtu-ignore' as a workaround but fix the underlying MTU.

Layer-1 errors (CRC, runts, drops) on the transit interface also cause flaps - inspect 'show interfaces' counters and replace cabling or SFPs as needed.
symptoms: Packet loss on routes via affected neighbor

fixSteps.title: Check neighbor state
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show ip ospf neighbor' and 'show ip ospf interface <intf>' on both routers.

fixSteps.title: Verify MTU
fixSteps.instruction: Compare 'show interface | inc MTU' on both ends - mismatch causes EXSTART hangs.

fixSteps.title: Inspect L1 errors
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show interfaces <intf>' and look for CRC, input errors, drops; replace cable/SFP if non-zero.

fixSteps.title: Match timers
fixSteps.instruction: Set matching 'ip ospf hello-interval' and 'ip ospf dead-interval' on both interfaces.

whenToCallPro: Engage TAC if flaps continue after L1 and config verification.

faq.q: How do I know if MTU is the cause?
faq.a: Adjacency hangs in EXSTART or EXCHANGE then resets - classic MTU mismatch signature.
It hides the problem but may cause black holes for large packets - fix MTU instead.

title: PoE budget exceeded - power denied to port
shortDescription: A PoE port refused to power a connected device because the chassis power budget is full.
fullDescription:
Catalyst PoE switches allocate power from a finite budget set by the installed PSU. When demand exceeds budget, new powered devices are denied with %ILPOWER-5-POWER_DENIED. The port LED shows amber instead of green.

Run 'show power inline' to see allocated vs available watts. Options: install a higher-wattage PSU (or second PSU for redundancy), reduce per-port allocation with 'power inline auto max <mW>', or set port priority so critical devices keep power.

On 9300-PWR series, upgrading from 715W to 1100W PSU adds ~385W of usable PoE budget.

causes.cause: Sum of connected PD demand exceeds PSU budget
Single PSU on dual-PSU model halves budget

symptoms: 'show power inline' shows 0W on the port

fixSteps.title: Check budget
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show power inline' to see total/used/available watts.

fixSteps.title: Add or upgrade PSU
fixSteps.instruction: Install second PSU or upgrade to higher wattage to expand budget.

fixSteps.title: Cap per-port power
fixSteps.instruction: Use 'power inline auto max <mW>' to limit allocations and free budget.

fixSteps.title: Set priorities
fixSteps.instruction: Use 'power inline port priority high' on critical PDs so they keep power if budget tightens.

whenToCallPro: If a higher PSU is unavailable for the platform, professional design review may be needed.

faq.q: Can I run two PSUs in load-share mode?
faq.a: Yes - 'power supply autoLC' enables combined budget instead of redundancy.

faq.q: What's the difference between 802.3af, at, bt?
faq.a: af = 15.4W, at = 30W, bt = 60-90W per port - the PD negotiates its class.

title: Smart Licensing evaluation expired
shortDescription: The 90-day Smart Licensing evaluation has expired and the device is enforced or out of compliance.
fullDescription:
Catalyst 9000 and IOS-XE devices use Cisco Smart Licensing. After 90 days without registration to a Smart Account, evaluation expires and the device enters Out-of-Compliance (or Enforced on 17.3.2+). Some features (HSEC, advanced routing) may stop working.

Register via direct internet, on-prem CSSM (Smart Software Manager On-Prem), or CSLU (Cisco Smart Licensing Utility). Generate a token in https://software.cisco.com, then on the device run 'license smart trust idtoken <token> all'.

For air-gapped networks, use Specific License Reservation (SLR) - generate a request code, redeem it on CSSM, and install the authorization code with 'license smart reservation install <auth>'.

causes.cause: Device never registered to a Smart Account
Device cannot reach tools.cisco.com or CSSM

fixSteps.title: Generate token
fixSteps.instruction: In Smart Software Manager (software.cisco.com) generate an instance token for your virtual account.

fixSteps.title: Verify connectivity
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm device can reach tools.cisco.com:443 (or CSSM On-Prem URL).

fixSteps.title: Register device
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'license smart trust idtoken <token> all' from privileged exec.

fixSteps.title: Verify status
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show license status' - should show 'AUTHORIZED' or 'IN COMPLIANCE'.

whenToCallPro: Smart Account access issues - engage Cisco licensing TAC.

faq.q: Will the device stop forwarding when EVAL expires?
faq.a: On most platforms no - but enforced features (HSEC, AppX) get disabled.
Yes - Specific License Reservation (SLR) for air-gapped networks.

title: Port err-disabled by storm-control
shortDescription: An interface entered err-disabled state because broadcast/multicast/unicast traffic exceeded the configured storm-control threshold.
fullDescription:
Storm control monitors per-port broadcast, multicast, or unknown-unicast rates. When the configured threshold is exceeded, the port is shut down (err-disabled) to protect the switch fabric. Common triggers: a network loop, a faulty NIC flooding broadcasts, or a misbehaving IoT device.

Identify the port with 'show interfaces status err-disabled'. The cause column shows 'storm-control'. Recover with 'shutdown' / 'no shutdown' or enable 'errdisable recovery cause storm-control' for automatic recovery after 300 seconds.

Address the root cause - sniff with 'monitor session' or check 'show storm-control' counters before the port flaps again.
symptoms: Port LED off after brief amber

fixSteps.title: Identify port and cause
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show interfaces status err-disabled' and 'show errdisable recovery'.

fixSteps.title: Inspect traffic
fixSteps.instruction: Check 'show storm-control <intf>' for which traffic type tripped and at what rate.

fixSteps.title: Locate loop or bad device
fixSteps.instruction: Check spanning-tree topology, disconnect suspect device, look at broadcast counters.

fixSteps.title: Recover port
fixSteps.instruction: On the interface: 'shutdown' then 'no shutdown'. Optionally enable auto-recovery.

whenToCallPro: Repeated storms across multiple ports may indicate a design issue requiring a network architect review.

faq.a: Yes when combined with fixing root cause - prevents 3 AM truck rolls but can mask loops.
1-5% broadcast level is typical; tune based on baseline traffic measurements.

title: PortFast port shut by BPDU Guard
shortDescription: An access port configured with BPDU Guard received a BPDU and was err-disabled to prevent a loop.
fullDescription:
BPDU Guard protects PortFast-enabled access ports from accidental switch connections. If any BPDU arrives on such a port, the switch immediately err-disables it. Common cause: a user plugging a small unmanaged switch or an unauthorized switch into a wall jack.

The error appears as %SPANTREE-2-BLOCK_BPDUGUARD in syslog and the port shows 'err-disabled' with cause 'bpduguard'. Recover with shut/no shut after removing the offending device, or enable 'errdisable recovery cause bpduguard'.

If the connected device is legitimate (e.g., a known managed switch), reconfigure the port without 'spanning-tree portfast' and 'spanning-tree bpduguard enable'.

causes.cause: User plugged unauthorized switch into access port
PortFast misconfigured on uplink to another switch
Endpoint NIC sending malformed frames seen as BPDUs

fixSteps.title: Identify port
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'show interfaces status err-disabled' and locate cause 'bpduguard'.

fixSteps.title: Investigate physical
fixSteps.instruction: Walk to the wall jack or check cable map - look for a small unmanaged switch.

fixSteps.title: Remove offender or reconfigure
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the unauthorized switch, or if legitimate, remove portfast/bpduguard from interface config.

fixSteps.title: Recover port
fixSteps.instruction: On the interface: 'shutdown' then 'no shutdown' to bring it back up.

whenToCallPro: If repeated BPDU Guard trips occur across many ports, conduct an L2 design audit.

faq.q: Is BPDU Guard the same as Root Guard?
faq.a: No - BPDU Guard shuts the port on any BPDU; Root Guard only blocks superior BPDUs.
No - it's a key loop-prevention feature. Address the root cause instead.
